prop_desc: AMENDMENT TO PERMIT SALE OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES IN 'MINI-BOTTLES' AS SUBSTITUTE FOR 'BROWN-BAGGING' PLAN
notes_endorse: Editorial 'In Favor Of The Mini-Bottle' (Oct 31, 1972) — strongly supports amendment. 'We're in favor of the amendment which would make the so called mini-bottle plan possible.' Argues brown-bagging provision is 'just plain inexcusable, antiquated, and unrealistic.' Cites Orangeburg County attorney Thomas B. Bryant III in support.

prop_desc: AIKEN COUNTY HOSPITAL BOND REFERENDUM — $7,000,000 general obligation bonds for public hospital facilities
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) and 'The Hospital Vote' (Nov 4, 1974) — both editorials OPPOSE the hospital bonds. Reasoning: a YES vote means a public hospital with tax increase; a NO vote allows a private hospital (HCA) to be built within 18 months without raising taxes. 'We have previously made clear our recommendation that voters cast their ballots as OPPOSED TO BONDS.' (NOTE: original extraction created two contradictory rows for this single proposition; consolidated to single OPPOSED row in re-QA 2026-05-26.)

prop_desc: HORSE CREEK BASIN WASTEWATER TREATMENT FACILITY — authorizing Aiken County Board of Commissioners to acquire, construct, and operate facility (treatment plant, trunk lines, connector lines) using federal and state grants, with no tax increase
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'The second most important issue to local residents will be the question of authorizing the Horse Creek Basin Wastewater Treatment Facility... When completed, this facility will serve a wide area — all the way from North Augusta to the City of Aiken — and will take care of our wastewater problems for many years. We strongly urge a YES vote on this highly important issue.' (NOTE: this endorsement was completely missing from the original extraction; added in re-QA 2026-05-26.)
